rules.title: Ban on nonrefundable security deposits
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not contain a provision characterizing any security as nonrefundable.
rules.coverage_text: Residential leases and rental agreements subject to this section.
rules.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5(n) (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340, Sec. 1 (AB 414))
rules.penalty: Bad faith claim or retention of the security in violation of this section may subject the landlord or successors in interest to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.
rules.quoted_span: (n) A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

rules.title: Transfer or return of security deposit on termination of landlord's interest
rules.requirement: When the landlord's interest in the premises ends, the landlord must within a reasonable time either transfer the remaining security to the successor in interest and notify the tenant, or return the remaining security to the tenant with an accounting. If this is not done, the successors in interest are jointly and severally liable with the landlord for repayment of the security.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords holding a tenant's security whose interest in the premises terminates by sale, assignment, death, appointment of receiver, or otherwise, and their successors in interest.
rules.exemptions: A successor in interest with a good faith belief, after inquiry and reasonable investigation, that the remaining deposit was transferred or returned is not liable for damages under subdivision (m) or for security not transferred.
rules.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5(i)-(k) (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340, Sec. 1 (AB 414))
rules.penalty: Successors in interest jointly and severally liable for repayment of the security; bad faith demand of replacement security may subject the landlord or successors to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.
